name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBES_IN_HUMAN_WELFARE_MCQ_Q01 - Microbes in curd, dosa, idli, and bread

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the role of microbes in household food products:

Statement I: Lactobacillus and other lactic acid bacteria (LAB) grow in milk and convert it into curd by producing acids that coagulate and partially digest milk proteins.

Statement II: Curd improves nutritional quality by increasing vitamin B12, and LAB also play a beneficial role in checking disease-causing microbes in our stomach.

Statement III: The puffed-up appearance of dough used for making dosa and idli is due to CO2 production by Propionibacterium sharmanii.

Statement IV: The dough used for making bread is fermented using baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae).

Which of the above statements are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Household fermentation processes rely on specific bacteria and yeasts to alter texture, digestibility, and nutritional value of dairy and cereal-based foods.

Step 2: Evaluation of Curd Formation and LAB Benefits
Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) such as Lactobacillus multiply in milk at suitable temperatures, producing acids that coagulate and partially digest milk proteins to form curd. This enhances vitamin B12 content, and LAB also inhibit disease-causing microbes in the human stomach. Hence, both claims regarding curd formation, vitamin B12 enrichment, and stomach protection are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Dosa, Idli, and Bread Fermentation
The dough for dosa and idli is fermented by bacteria that release CO2 gas, whereas Propionibacterium sharmanii is the bacterium responsible for producing large holes in Swiss cheese, not dosa or idli dough. Meanwhile, bread dough is fermented using baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae). Thus, the claim attributing dosa and idli fermentation to Propionibacterium sharmanii is incorrect, while the claim regarding baker's yeast in bread-making is correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims concerning lactic acid bacteria in curd formation, vitamin B12 enhancement and gut protection, and baker's yeast in bread dough are correct, whereas the claim linking Propionibacterium sharmanii to dosa and idli dough is incorrect.

answer.text: I, II, III, and IV are all correct
Only I and II are correct
I, II, and IV are correct, whereas III is incorrect
I, III, and IV are correct, whereas II is incorrect

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBES_IN_HUMAN_WELFARE_MCQ_Q02 - Fermented beverages and discovery of penicillin

questiontext.text:
Examine the following four statements about industrial fermented beverages and antibiotics:

Statement I: Brewer's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) is used for fermenting malted cereals and fruit juices to produce ethanol.

Statement II: Wine and beer are produced without distillation, whereas whisky, brandy, and rum are produced by distillation of the fermented broth.

Statement III: Alexander Fleming discovered Penicillin by chance while working on Staphylococci bacteria, and its full potential as an effective antibiotic was later established by Ernest Chain and Howard Florey.

Statement IV: Fleming, Chain, and Florey were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1945 for the discovery and development of Penicillin.

Choose the correct option:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Industrial microbiology encompasses large-scale ethanol fermentation for alcoholic beverages as well as the discovery and clinical development of life-saving antibiotics.

Step 2: Evaluation of Fermented Beverages
Saccharomyces cerevisiae, known as brewer's yeast, ferments malted cereals and fruit juices to produce ethanol. Depending on processing, wine and beer are obtained without distillation, while whisky, brandy, and rum are produced by distilling the fermented broth. Thus, both claims regarding beverage fermentation and distillation are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Penicillin Discovery and Recognition
Alexander Fleming discovered Penicillin serendipitously when a mould, Penicillium notatum, inhibited the growth of Staphylococci on an unwashed culture plate. Later, Ernest Chain and Howard Florey established its full potential as an effective antibiotic, and all three were awarded the Nobel Prize in 1945. Thus, both claims regarding Penicillin's discovery, development, and Nobel recognition are correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
All four propositions concerning brewer's yeast, distillation of alcoholic drinks, the roles of Fleming, Chain, and Florey, and the 1945 Nobel Prize are factually accurate.

answer.text: All four statements I, II, III, and IV are correct
Only I, II, and III are correct
Only I, III, and IV are correct
Only II and III are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBES_IN_HUMAN_WELFARE_MCQ_Q03 - Industrial organic acids, enzymes, and bioactive molecules

questiontext.text:
Evaluate the following four statements regarding microbial chemicals, enzymes, and bioactive molecules:

Statement I: Aspergillus niger is used to produce citric acid, and Clostridium butylicum is used to produce butyric acid.

Statement II: Lipases are used in detergent formulations to remove oily stains, whereas pectinases and proteases clarify bottled fruit juices.

Statement III: Cyclosporin A, obtained from the fungus Trichoderma polysporum, is used as a 'clot buster' for removing clots from blood vessels of myocardial infarction patients.

Statement IV: Statins produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus act as blood-cholesterol lowering agents by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for cholesterol synthesis.

Which of the following is the correct assessment?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Micro-organisms synthesise diverse organic acids, hydrolytic enzymes, and bioactive pharmaceuticals with distinct industrial and medical applications.

Step 2: Evaluation of Acid Producers and Commercial Enzymes
Aspergillus niger (a fungus) produces citric acid and Clostridium butylicum (a bacterium) produces butyric acid. In industry, lipases are incorporated into detergents to break down oily stains, while pectinases and proteases clarify bottled fruit juices. Hence, both claims regarding acid producers and commercial enzymes are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Bioactive Molecules
Cyclosporin A from Trichoderma polysporum is used as an immunosuppressive agent in organ-transplant patients; it is streptokinase (produced by Streptococcus and genetically modified) that functions as a clot buster in myocardial infarction patients. Therefore, attributing clot-busting activity to cyclosporin A is incorrect. Meanwhile, statins from Monascus purpureus lower blood cholesterol by competitively inhibiting the cholesterol-synthesising enzyme, making the statin claim correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding citric and butyric acid producers, lipases, pectinases, proteases, and statins are correct, whereas the claim describing cyclosporin A as a clot buster is incorrect.

answer.text: All four statements I, II, III, and IV are correct
I, II, and IV are correct, whereas III is incorrect
I, III, and IV are correct, whereas II is incorrect
Only II and IV are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBES_IN_HUMAN_WELFARE_MCQ_Q04 - Primary and secondary sewage treatment stages

questiontext.text:
Read the following four statements regarding municipal sewage treatment:

Statement I: Primary treatment involves physical removal of floating debris by sequential filtration and grit by sedimentation, yielding primary sludge and primary effluent.

Statement II: In aeration tanks, mechanical agitation and air pumping support vigorous growth of aerobic microbes into mesh-like structures called flocs, which consume organic matter.

Statement III: The greater the biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) of waste water, the lower is its polluting potential.

Statement IV: Once BOD is reduced, bacterial flocs sediment in a settling tank to form activated sludge, a small fraction of which is pumped back into the aeration tank as inoculum.

Select the correct option:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Sewage treatment combines physical separation during primary treatment with aerobic microbial oxidation during secondary treatment to reduce organic load before discharge.

Step 2: Evaluation of Primary Treatment and Flocs
During primary treatment, sequential filtration removes floating debris and sedimentation removes grit, producing settled primary sludge and liquid effluent. In secondary aeration tanks, constant agitation and aeration promote aerobic microbial flocs (bacteria associated with fungal filaments) that consume organic matter. Thus, both claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of BOD and Activated Sludge
Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) measures the oxygen required to oxidise organic matter in one litre of water; higher BOD reflects greater organic pollution and therefore a higher—not lower—polluting potential. Consequently, claiming that higher BOD means lower polluting potential is incorrect. After BOD drops, flocs settle as activated sludge, and a small portion is returned to the aeration tank as inoculum, making the activated sludge claim correct.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims describing primary filtration/sedimentation, aerobic flocs, and activated sludge recycling are correct, whereas the claim equating higher BOD with lower polluting potential is incorrect.

answer.text: I, II, and III are correct, whereas IV is incorrect
II, III, and IV are correct, whereas I is incorrect
All four statements I, II, III, and IV are correct
I, II, and IV are correct, whereas III is incorrect

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBES_IN_HUMAN_WELFARE_MCQ_Q05 - Anaerobic digesters, river action plans, and methanogens

questiontext.text:
Analyse the following four statements about anaerobic digestion, river conservation, and methanogens:

Statement I: In anaerobic sludge digesters, anaerobic bacteria digest the bacteria and fungi in the sludge, generating a mixture of methane, hydrogen sulphide, and carbon dioxide.

Statement II: The Ministry of Environment and Forests initiated the Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan to build sewage treatment plants so that only treated sewage is discharged into these rivers.

Statement III: Methanogens like Methanobacterium grow anaerobically on cellulosic material in the rumen of cattle, helping in cellulose breakdown and cattle nutrition.

Statement IV: Human beings are able to digest the cellulose present in their plant foods efficiently because human intestines harbour large populations of Methanobacterium.

Which of the following is true?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Anaerobic bacteria convert organic sludge and cellulosic waste into biogas, while river action plans aim to expand sewage treatment infrastructure to curb water pollution.

Step 2: Evaluation of Anaerobic Digestion and River Action Plans
In anaerobic sludge digesters, anaerobic bacteria digest the microbial biomass in activated sludge to produce inflammable biogas containing methane, hydrogen sulphide, and carbon dioxide. Furthermore, the Ministry of Environment and Forests launched the Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan to construct additional STPs so only treated sewage enters these rivers. Both claims are therefore correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Methanogens in Cattle vs Humans
Methanogens such as Methanobacterium grow anaerobically on cellulosic material in the rumen of cattle, assisting in cellulose digestion and cattle nutrition. In contrast, human beings are unable to digest cellulose present in food. Thus, the claim regarding methanogens in the cattle rumen is correct, whereas the claim that humans digest cellulose efficiently via intestinal Methanobacterium is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims concerning anaerobic sludge digesters, the Ganga and Yamuna Action Plans, and methanogens in the cattle rumen are correct, while the claim regarding human cellulose digestion is incorrect.

answer.text: I, II, and III are correct, whereas IV is incorrect
I, III, and IV are correct, whereas II is incorrect
II, III, and IV are correct, whereas I is incorrect
All four statements I, II, III, and IV are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MICROBES_IN_HUMAN_WELFARE_MCQ_Q06 - Biogas plant design and predatory biocontrol insects

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding biogas plants and biological pest control:

Statement I: A biogas plant consists of a 10–15 feet deep concrete tank fed with bio-wastes and dung slurry, topped by a floating cover that rises as gas is produced.

Statement II: In India, biogas production technology was developed mainly by IARI and KVIC, and the spent slurry is removed to be used as fertiliser.

Statement III: Organic farmers believe that biodiversity furthers health and keep pests at manageable levels through ecological checks and balances rather than eradicating them.

Statement IV: The Ladybird beetle is useful to get rid of mosquitoes, whereas Dragonflies are useful to get rid of aphids.

Which of the following options is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biogas plants harness anaerobic digestion for rural fuel and fertiliser, while organic farming uses natural predation to regulate pest populations sustainably.

Step 2: Evaluation of Biogas Plant Structure and Development
A typical biogas plant has a concrete tank (10–15 feet deep) receiving bio-wastes and dung slurry, with a floating cover that rises as microbial gas accumulates; spent slurry is recovered as fertiliser. The technology was developed in India largely by the Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC). Hence, both biogas claims are correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Organic Farming and Insect Predators
Organic farmers maintain biodiversity and manage pests via natural checks and balances rather than seeking total eradication, which would starve beneficial predators and parasites. However, it is the Ladybird beetle that controls aphids and Dragonflies that control mosquitoes—not the reverse. Thus, the ecological philosophy claim is correct, while the swapped predator-prey claim is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding biogas plant operation, IARI/KVIC contributions and spent slurry, and the organic farming approach to pest management are correct, whereas the claim reversing the prey of Ladybird beetles and Dragonflies is incorrect.

answer.text: I, II, and IV are correct, whereas III is incorrect
I, III, and IV are correct, whereas II is incorrect
I, II, and III are correct, whereas IV is incorrect
All four statements I, II, III, and IV are correct

questiontext.text:
Examine the following four statements about microbial biocontrol agents:

Statement I: Dried spores of Bacillus thuringiensis sprayed onto brassicas and fruit trees are eaten by insect larvae, releasing a toxin in the larval gut that kills caterpillars while leaving other insects unharmed.

Statement II: Trichoderma species are free-living fungi common in root ecosystems that act as effective biocontrol agents against several plant pathogens.

Statement III: Baculoviruses in the genus Nucleopolyhedrovirus are species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticides with no negative impacts on plants, mammals, birds, fish, or non-target insects.

Statement IV: Because Nucleopolyhedrovirus agents harm beneficial insects, they are avoided in Integrated Pest Management (IPM) programmes.

Which of the following is the correct evaluation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Microbial biocontrol agents—including bacteria, fungi, and viruses—offer targeted suppression of agricultural pests and plant pathogens while safeguarding non-target organisms.

Step 2: Evaluation of Bacillus thuringiensis and Trichoderma
Bacillus thuringiensis spores ingested by insect larvae release a gut toxin that kills caterpillars without harming other insects. Similarly, Trichoderma species are free-living root-ecosystem fungi effective against several plant pathogens. Both claims are therefore correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Baculoviruses and IPM
Nucleopolyhedrovirus baculoviruses are species-specific, narrow-spectrum insecticidal agents shown to have no negative effects on plants, mammals, birds, fish, or non-target insects. Precisely because they conserve beneficial insects, they are especially desirable—not avoided—in Integrated Pest Management (IPM) programmes and ecologically sensitive areas. Thus, the host-specificity claim is correct, while the claim that they harm beneficial insects and are avoided in IPM is incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding Bacillus thuringiensis, Trichoderma, and the narrow-spectrum safety of Nucleopolyhedrovirus are correct, whereas the claim that Nucleopolyhedrovirus harms beneficial insects and is avoided in IPM is incorrect.

answer.text: All four statements I, II, III, and IV are correct
I, II, and III are correct, whereas IV is incorrect
I, III, and IV are correct, whereas II is incorrect
II, III, and IV are correct, whereas I is incorrect

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding microbes used as biofertilisers:

Statement I: Rhizobium forms symbiotic nodules on the roots of leguminous plants and fixes atmospheric nitrogen into organic forms used as nutrient by the plant.

Statement II: Free-living soil bacteria such as Azospirillum and Azotobacter fix atmospheric nitrogen, enriching the nitrogen content of the soil.

Statement III: Many members of the fungal genus Glomus form mycorrhiza, absorbing phosphorus from soil for the plant and conferring resistance to root-borne pathogens, salinity, and drought.

Statement IV: Cyanobacteria such as Anabaena, Nostoc, and Oscillatoria are heterotrophic microbes unable to fix atmospheric nitrogen in paddy fields.

Select the correct option:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Biofertilisers are bacteria, fungi, and cyanobacteria that enrich soil nutrient quality and promote sustainable crop growth without chemical pollution.

Step 2: Evaluation of Nitrogen-Fixing Bacteria and Mycorrhiza
Rhizobium symbiotically fixes atmospheric nitrogen in legume root nodules, while free-living bacteria like Azospirillum and Azotobacter enrich soil nitrogen independently. Fungi of the genus Glomus form mycorrhizal associations that supply phosphorus to plants while enhancing resistance to root-borne pathogens, salinity, and drought, and boosting overall growth. All three claims are therefore correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Cyanobacteria
Cyanobacteria such as Anabaena, Nostoc, and Oscillatoria are autotrophic—not heterotrophic—microbes that fix atmospheric nitrogen, add organic matter to soil, and serve as major biofertilisers in paddy fields. Claiming they are heterotrophic and unable to fix nitrogen is therefore incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The claims regarding symbiotic Rhizobium, free-living Azospirillum and Azotobacter, and Glomus mycorrhiza are correct, whereas the claim describing cyanobacteria as heterotrophic non-fixers is incorrect.

answer.text: All four statements I, II, III, and IV are correct
I, II, and IV are correct, whereas III is incorrect
II, III, and IV are correct, whereas I is incorrect
I, II, and III are correct, whereas IV is incorrect
